title: Polymorphic Error Correction
problem: Traditional memory error correction codes target single fault models or require multiple redundancies for multi-fault support, leading to higher storage overhead. Systems need efficient error correction that simultaneously handles single-bit, double-bit, and ChipKill faults without excessive redundancy.
motivation: Reducing error correction redundancy overhead while supporting multiple fault models improves memory efficiency and system reliability.
method: Polymorphic ECC employs redundancy polymorphism where the same check bits correct errors from different fault models (single-bit, double-bit, ChipKill, etc.). An inlined cryptographic MAC is embedded with each cacheline for data integrity. Iterative correction is applied across supported fault models, using up to 60-bit MACs with 64-byte cachelines over standard 40-bit DDR5 memory channels.
key_novelty: Redundancy polymorphism allows the same check bits to correct multiple types of errors rather than requiring separate redundancies for each fault model.
contributions: Novel redundancy polymorphism concept enabling multi-fault-model error correction
Compact embedded inlined cryptographic MAC for data integrity without extra storage overhead
Iterative correction mechanism across multiple fault models with near 100% error detection
Support for correcting fault models not covered by traditional error correction codes

metrics.other: Corrects more fault models than traditional codes

limitations: Specific performance, energy, and area overhead metrics compared to traditional ECC schemes not discussed.
primary_theme: Memory error correction with polymorphic redundancy
